title: Email Delivery
summary: Sending email is easy; getting it into the inbox is not. Receiving servers like Gmail judge every message by who sent it and how that sender has behaved. A delivery system authenticates mail with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, sends from IPs and domains with a good reputation, paces traffic to each mailbox provider, and listens closely to bounces and spam complaints, removing bad addresses before they damage reputation.

walkthrough.title: App sends an email
walkthrough.text: The app calls the email API: send a password-reset template to jane@gmail.com with the message ID as an idempotency key.

walkthrough.title: Check suppression
walkthrough.text: The API checks a suppression list. Addresses that hard-bounced, complained, or unsubscribed are skipped. Sending to them is the fastest way to ruin reputation.

walkthrough.title: Sign and queue
walkthrough.text: The message is rendered, DKIM-signed with the sending domain's private key, and queued per destination domain on a mail transfer agent (MTA).

walkthrough.title: Deliver over SMTP
walkthrough.text: The MTA looks up gmail.com's MX records, connects over TLS, and hands the message off, pacing connections per provider and retrying 4xx deferrals with backoff for up to days.

walkthrough.title: Receiver verifies the sender
walkthrough.text: Gmail checks SPF (is this IP allowed to send for the domain?), DKIM (is the signature valid?), and DMARC (do they align with the From: domain, and what is the policy if not?), all published in the sender's DNS.

walkthrough.title: Bounces and complaints come back
walkthrough.text: Hard bounces (no such user), soft bounces, spam complaints via feedback loops, and daily DMARC aggregate reports flow back to the sender.

walkthrough.title: Suppress and adjust
walkthrough.text: Bad addresses are suppressed immediately, complaint rates are watched (keep below about 0.1%), and sending is throttled if a provider starts deferring.

data.label: Application
responsibilities: Sends only to people who expect the email.
Separates transactional mail (password reset) from marketing.
Includes one-click unsubscribe on bulk mail.

failureModes.scenario: Marketing and transactional mail share a domain/IP
failureModes.impact: A spammy campaign stops password resets from arriving.
failureModes.mitigation: Separate subdomains and IP pools per mail stream.
Opt-in only; confirm sign-ups; sunset inactive addresses.

data.label: Email API
responsibilities: Validates addresses and checks suppression before sending.
Renders templates and signs with DKIM.
Enforces per-account sending limits.

failureModes.mitigation: Content scanning, anomaly detection, automatic pausing.

data.label: Suppression List
responsibilities: Blocks sends to known-bad or opted-out addresses.
Updates immediately on bounces and complaints.
Honours legal unsubscribe requirements.

failureModes.scenario: Suppression check skipped on a code path
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce in the API layer, not in each caller.
Suppress soft bounces only after repeated failures; allow removal.

data.label: MTA Fleet

output.name: SMTP
output.type: MAIL FROM / RCPT TO / DATA over STARTTLS

responsibilities: Delivers to each provider at a rate it accepts.
Retries temporary failures for up to ~72 hours.
Warms up new IPs gradually to build reputation.

failureModes.mitigation: Back off for that domain; reduce concurrency; investigate reputation.

failureModes.scenario: New IP sends full volume on day one

data.label: Sender DNS Records
responsibilities: Publishes which servers may send for the domain (SPF).
Publishes DKIM public keys for signature checks.
Tells receivers what to do with unauthenticated mail (DMARC).

failureModes.impact: SPF fails; mail goes to spam.
failureModes.mitigation: Flatten includes; use subdomains per sending service.

failureModes.scenario: DMARC p=reject before all senders are aligned
failureModes.impact: Legitimate mail from a forgotten tool is rejected.
failureModes.mitigation: Start at p=none, read reports, then tighten.

data.label: Mailbox Providers
responsibilities: Authenticate senders and score reputation and content.
Decide inbox or spam placement.
Report complaints back through feedback loops.

failureModes.impact: Bulk mail rejected (required by Gmail and Yahoo since 2024).
failureModes.mitigation: SPF + DKIM + DMARC aligned, plus one-click unsubscribe.

failureModes.impact: Domain reputation drops; everything lands in spam.
failureModes.mitigation: Monitor Postmaster Tools; send only wanted mail.

data.label: Bounces & Feedback

input.name: Signals
input.type: DSN bounces, ARF complaints, DMARC XML

responsibilities: Classifies bounces (hard vs soft) and complaints.
Feeds the suppression list immediately.
Tracks reputation metrics per domain and IP.

failureModes.mitigation: Use standard DSN codes; review unclassified bounces.

failureModes.impact: Spoofing of your domain goes unnoticed.
failureModes.mitigation: Process aggregate reports; alert on unknown senders.
